mainTopic: Can heating (היסק) clean what an earthenware vessel absorbed? Questions from the Temple's pots and the Temple's oven
overview: The גמרא is testing the view that heating (היסק) an earthenware vessel cleans out what it absorbed. First it asks: if heating works, why does the תורה say the earthenware pots of the מקדש must be broken? Why not just re-fire them in a kiln? רבי זירא answers that kilns are not built in ירושלים. אביי objects that scrap heaps are not allowed in the עזרה either, so where would the broken pieces go? The גמרא answers that אביי forgot שמעיה's teaching: broken pottery in the מקדש was miraculously swallowed up where it lay. Then the גמרא asks a second question: why was the oven of the מקדש made of metal, when an earthenware oven heated from inside would clean itself? The answer is that the oven bakes the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים and makes them holy, so it is a כלי שרת. A כלי שרת is never made of earthenware.

steps.title: Why break the Temple pots instead of re-firing them?
steps.stepSummary: If heating cleans earthenware, the תורה's command to break the Temple's earthenware pots seems unnecessary. Just put them back in a kiln.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the pots of the מקדש: why did the תורה say they must be broken? Let us just put them back into the kilns!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that heating cleans earthenware. It points to the פסוק that says the Temple's earthenware pots must be broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kiln heats a pot from the inside and the outside with very strong heat. If heat can clean out what a pot absorbed, the pots of קדשים should be re-fired and saved, not smashed. Since the תורה says to break them, maybe heat does not clean earthenware.

keyTerms.meaning: Pots, here the earthenware pots used for cooking קדשים
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Kilns, the very hot furnaces where pottery is fired

phrases.english: But the pots of the Temple
why did the Merciful One say "they should be broken"?
Let us return them to the kilns!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קְדֵירוֹת שֶׁל מִקְדָּשׁ אַמַּאי אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא יִשָּׁבְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view, from the earlier part of the sugya, that heating cleans earthenware.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that היסק cleans out what earthenware absorbed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If heat cleans earthenware, the פסוק commanding the pots be broken is pointless, because re-firing them would be enough.

steps.title: No kilns are allowed in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the pots could not be re-fired, because kilns may not be built in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Because kilns are not made in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. He says the pots are broken because there is nowhere in ירושלים to re-fire them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps the idea that heating works. The problem is only practical: kilns are not allowed in ירושלים, so re-firing is not an option. That is why the תורה says to break the pots.

keyTerms.meaning: ירושלים, where special rules apply, including a ban on kilns

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Because they do not make kilns in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין כִּבְשׁוֹנוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical limitation: the cleaning method works, but it cannot be done in that place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Re-firing in a kiln could save the pots.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are no kilns in ירושלים, so the pots must be broken.

steps.title: אביי: then where do the broken pieces go?
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects to רבי זירא: scrap heaps are not allowed either, so what is done with the broken pottery in the Temple courtyard?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: But do they make scrap heaps in the עזרה?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי זירא's answer. If the same rules ban garbage heaps, breaking the pots just leaves broken pieces with nowhere to go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא relied on a rule about what may not be built in ירושלים. אביי points out that the same set of rules also bans scrap heaps. So breaking the pots creates a new problem: the pieces would pile up in the עזרה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
But do they make scrap heaps in the Temple courtyard?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי וְכִי עוֹשִׂין אַשְׁפַּתּוֹת בָּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's answer that the pots are broken because there are no kilns
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scrap heaps are banned too, so breaking the pots leaves pieces with nowhere to go. The no-kilns rule does not settle the matter.

steps.title: The broken pieces were swallowed up by a miracle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי forgot a teaching of שמעיה: in the Temple, broken earthenware was swallowed up right where it lay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what שמעיה taught in קלנבו: The broken pieces of earthenware vessels are swallowed up in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns away אביי's objection. It quotes a teaching that broken pottery in the Temple disappeared into the ground right where it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was never a scrap heap problem, because the shards vanished by a miracle. So רבי זירא's answer still works: there are no kilns to re-fire the pots, so they are broken, and the pieces take care of themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: It slipped his mind; he forgot
שמעיה of the place called קלנבו, who taught this ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The pots of קדשים are broken because there are no kilns in ירושלים to re-fire them, and the broken pieces were miraculously swallowed up, so no scrap heap was needed.

phrases.english: That which Shemaya taught in Kalnevo escaped him:
Shards of earthenware vessels
are swallowed up in their place.
phrases.notes: The broken pieces sank into the ground right there in the Temple, by a miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away אביי's objection in step 3 and keeps רבי זירא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Quotes a forgotten ברייתא that removes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Breaking the pots would leave a pile of shards in the עזרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shards were miraculously swallowed up, so no scrap heap was ever needed.

steps.title: Why was the Temple oven made of metal?
steps.stepSummary: If heating from the inside cleans earthenware, why did the Temple use a metal oven? An earthenware oven heated from inside would clean itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the oven of the מקדש was made of metal. Let us make it of earthenware, since it is heated from the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the idea that heating cleans earthenware, this time from the Temple's oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven is always fired from the inside. If that heat cleans what earthenware absorbs, an earthenware oven would keep itself clean. So why did they need metal? This suggests the cleaning idea may be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Its heating (היסק) is from the inside

phrases.english: But that which Rav Nachman said
Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנּוּר שֶׁל מִקְדָּשׁ שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת הֲוָה
phrases.english: The oven of the Temple was of metal
Let us make it of earthenware
since its heating is from the inside!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, parallel to step 1, against the view that heating cleans earthenware.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that heating from inside cleans earthenware
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oven is heated from inside, so an earthenware oven would clean itself. The choice of metal suggests heating does not clean earthenware.

steps.title: The oven is a service vessel, and those are never earthenware
steps.stepSummary: The oven bakes and makes holy the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים, so it counts as a כלי שרת. A כלי שרת is never made of earthenware.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there are the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים, which are baked in the oven and become holy in the oven, the oven is a כלי שרת. And we do not make a כלי שרת out of earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the metal had nothing to do with cleaning. The oven had to be metal because it is a כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים become holy when they are placed in the oven, and that is what makes the oven a כלי שרת. A כלי שרת may not be made of earthenware, so the oven had to be metal for that reason. The idea that heating cleans earthenware stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed weekly on the שולחן
A service vessel of the Temple, which makes things holy

steps.whatToRemember: The Temple oven was metal not because of cleaning but because it was a כלי שרת, and a כלי שרת cannot be made of earthenware.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule can have a reason that has nothing to do with the topic being tested. The metal oven teaches about כלי שרת, not about היסק.

phrases.english: Because since there are
the Two Loaves and the Showbread
whose baking is in the oven
and whose sanctification is in the oven;
it is a service vessel,
and we do not make a service vessel of earthenware.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִיכָּא שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the metal oven
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oven was metal because earthenware cannot be cleaned by heating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oven was metal because it is a כלי שרת, and a כלי שרת is never made of earthenware.
